subtype: Approach: asking colleagues who moved before for advice [Thinking]
passage: Kashish had eleven days before his transfer to Hyderabad and a list of worries too long to fit on a phone screen. At lunch he asked two colleagues who had moved before, Jasleen and another, to spare twenty minutes. Jasleen went first. "Ask for the broker's fee up front and get it in writing. Don't pay it to more than one." The other colleague said school forms in that city had cut-off dates, and named two neighbourhoods where the water supply was unreliable. Kashish wrote it all in the back of his diary. With eleven days he could not test everything, but he crossed two listings off his list and asked the broker for the fee in writing. A month later a new coworker lost a deposit to the very trap Jasleen had described.

qa.q: What did Jasleen advise about the broker's fee?
qa.a: Jasleen said to ask for it up front, get it in writing, and not pay it to more than one broker.

qa.q: What was Kashish likely feeling as he wrote the advice in his diary?
qa.a: Kashish was probably anxious about the short time but relieved to have concrete tips.
Kashish could also ask someone already living near the new office and check details himself, rather than rely on one story.

qa.q: How might Jasleen have felt sharing the advice?
qa.a: Jasleen may have felt glad to spare Kashish mistakes that others had already made.

grounding: Kashish talks to two colleagues who relocated earlier and learns about broker fees, school timelines and areas to avoid.
